rationale: Das and Walton (2015) combine a random-sample survey of 1,200 households (plus local settlement census data) with longitudinal ethnographic interviews and court/documentary records (mixed_methods) to examine struggles over housing and urban infrastructure in two unplanned settlements in Delhi NCR (Punjabi Basti and NOIDA Sectors 5 and 8). Across both sites, eligibility_status_documentation is the single most central rule mechanism: unauthorized settlement status, contested land tenure, lack of sequential house addresses and official colony maps blocking utility metering in Punjabi Basti, and contested administrative rehabilitation surveys and residency documentation (ration cards, voter ID cards, composite-address electricity bills) in NOIDA. However, multiple distinct mechanisms operate as co-equally central exposures in the empirical analysis—including participation_assistance (registered societies and local political leaders navigating bureaucratic/municipal processes), review_redress (civil litigation against Ramjas Foundation and High Court writ petitions/stay orders against eviction and for alternate housing), enforcement_sanctions and regulatory_model_ownership (privatization of electricity into BSES triggering theft policing and subsequent meter regularization), and discretion_accommodation (utility and DDA officials guiding mapping and dual-address billing workarounds)—warranting 'multiple' for assigned_mechanism_label_with_multiple. Outcomes center primarily on administrative_outcome (emergence/fragmentation of local governance and leadership, court stay orders, municipal approval of an authorized colony map, provisional colony regularization, and contested survey/allotment approvals, alongside meter installation in Punjabi Basti while water/sewage projects remain unresolved).
